title: Target and Walmart Vendor Requirements: What Food Brands Need Before They Pitch
summary: Target and Walmart don't take pitches from just anyone. Here's what mass retail buyers expect from food brands before and after they earn a spot on shelf.
body_markdown:
[Tips](https://thefreshfactory.co/blog-categories/tips/)


August 10, 2026


There’s a clean-label, better-for-you revolution happening in CPG — and mass retailers like Target and Walmart are paying attention. In the first quarter of 2026, Target added more than[3,000 new food and beverage items,](https://www.thetakeout.com/2194896/target-grocery-shopping-changes-2026/) with a heavy tilt toward wellness. It also became the first national retailer to carry only cereal made without synthetic colors. Walmart, meanwhile, has[committed to eliminating synthetic dyes and 30 other ingredients](https://corporate.walmart.com/news/2025/10/01/walmart-u-s-moves-to-eliminate-synthetic-dyes-across-all-private-brand-food-products) from its private brand foods by January 2027.


The clean-label focus opens up new opportunities in mass retail for health-conscious CPG brands, but the requirements to actually get there haven’t gotten any easier. Here’s our primer for how to get your food brand into mass retailers like Target and Walmart.


## Earning the Buyer Meeting


Target runs a public[Supplier Intake Application,](https://corporate.target.com/sustainability-governance/responsible-supply-chains/suppliers/supplier-intake-form) while Walmart lets you self-register through[Retail Link](https://corporate.walmart.com/suppliers/apply-to-be-a-supplier) . But neither process is an open door, and applying won’t necessarily get you a meeting. A buyer connection through a broker, a trade event, or an existing relationship is still what tends to move a brand from the database into an actual conversation.


Unlike club stores that operate with a treasure hunt mentality, mass retailers follow rigid reset cycles for new product introductions, which require pitching the category buyer at the right time. .


Most planogram resets run two to four times a year depending on category speed, and fast-moving segments like snacks and beverages turn over more often than something like baking or cleaning. When a category comes up for review, buyers open a limited number of slots to existing and new vendors.


So how do you make sure you’re in the right place at the right time? Outside of building a relationship with a broker, you can look for events like Walmart’s[Annual Open Call](https://corporate.walmart.com/suppliers/investing-in-american-jobs/events/annual-open-call) , where SMBs can apply to meet directly with Walmart and Sam’s Club merchants. Target also runs two accelerator programs that can help brands get a foot in the door:[Forward Founders](https://accelerators.target.com/programs/target-forward-founders/) targets earlier-stage brands under five years old and under $10 million in revenue, while[Takeoff](https://accelerators.target.com/programs/target-takeoff/) is built for brands that already have some retail track record and want a structured path to scale with Target specifically.


Online marketplaces offered through mass retailers are also a good place to start; Target has Target Plus, the retailer’s invite-only third-party marketplace, and Walmart has Walmart Marketplace. Both are online-only and a different distribution model than earning a slot on a physical planogram, but they can allow you to build a sales history and brand awareness with customers.


## What to Expect with CPG Mass Retailers


Once you’ve earned the meeting, walking in with a rationale for why your product should displace something already on shelf, a promotional plan, and Nielsen or SPINS data showing velocity somewhere else is what separates a brand that gets a second call from one that doesn’t. It’s also crucial to have an understanding of the customer base and requirements of different vendors.


### Walmart Requirements


Walmart segments stores by demographics, ethnicity, income level, and other factors, and when buyers are looking for new products, they’re typically looking for more mainstream products that will sell well across certain segments. A brand getting into Walmart often doesn’t get all 4,500 supercenters — they might get 1,500 Class A stores, and SKU distribution can vary further within that.


In addition to making sure your pitch fits Walmart’s audience, you’ll need to take these requirements into consideration.


#### Certifications


GFSI certification is non-negotiable for mass retailers. Local, state, or federal food safety inspections won’t work — Walmart requires an independent GFSI-recognized audit. Having a facility that’s SQF-certified, like The Fresh Factory’s facilities, qualifies.


#### EDI Requirements


Walmart requires suppliers to exchange documents electronically over EDI (Electronic Data Interchange). At minimum brands must use the standardized EDI 850 Purchase Order, the 856 Advance Ship Notice, and the 810 Invoice. The 856 Advanced Ship Notice (ASN) is the most compliance-sensitive document in the set. It has to be transmitted and accepted before a shipment gates in at the distribution center, and it feeds directly into the OTIF scoring below.


#### Food Traceability


Traceability requirements tightened meaningfully in the last year. Since August 2025, Walmart has required food and beverage suppliers to align with[FSMA 204](https://www.fda.gov/food/food-safety-modernization-act-fsma/food-traceability-list) , meaning advance shipment notifications carrying the rule’s key data elements,[SSCC-18 barcodes](https://www.gs1us.org/upcs-barcodes-prefixes/serialized-shipping-container-codes) on pallets, and[GS1-128 barcodes](https://www.gs1us.org/upcs-barcodes-prefixes/gs1-128) on cases. Retail Link tracks this compliance directly now through a dedicated dashboard, and brands that lag are already being flagged inside it.


#### OTIF Requirements


OTIF (on time, in full) is where a lot of new suppliers get caught off guard. Walmart’s chargeback runs 3% of the cost of goods on non-compliant cases, with thresholds commonly set around 98% case-fill depending on category and freight arrangement. The failures typically come from a carrier missing an appointment window, a production run that ran long, an ingredient delay that forces a short-ship, or a routing guide requirement that got missed entirely. Walmart’s routing guide specifies exactly how a shipment has to move, and deviating from it triggers its own chargeback on top of any OTIF penalty.


####
Pallet Specs


Pallets follow a standard spec: 48×40 inches, 60 inches maximum height, stretch-wrapped.


### Target Requirements


Compared to Walmart, Target is more open to clean label, better-for-you products, and they also provide a more defined path for smaller brands with growth potential through their accelerator programs (mentioned above). However, there are some additional costs to getting your products on Target shelves.


#### Certifications


GFSI certification applies here too, and Target backs it with third-party audits and onsite risk assessments — mandatory for Target-branded products, and expected in practice for national brands as well.


#### EDI Requirements


EDI capability is required for orders, invoices, and other standard transactions — the same core document set Walmart requires. Target ties ASN (EDI 856) accuracy directly to a vendor performance program called Perfect Order, which checks compliance at two levels: item-level (does the case match the vendor case pack Target has on file?) and shipment-level (does the ASN match what’s actually on the truck?).


#### Food Traceability


Target’s ASN structure carries its own traceability backbone; SSCC-18 license-plate barcodes have to be carried through the shipment and match the case label, with the ASN itself structured hierarchically from pallet to case to item.


#### OTIF Requirements


Target calls this OTFR (On Time Fill Rate), measured against both on-time-arrival and on-time-ship targets, with deductions for vendors who fall short. A newer program called Perfect Order, which launched in 2025, added ASN accuracy on top of the fill-rate metric. Every non-compliant carton incurs a flat $0.75 fee with a $100 minimum.


#### Pallet & Case Packaging Specs


Target’s routing guide, published through the Partners Online portal, details the most up-to-date pallet and case specifics. Innerpacks are capped at 20x13x13 inches and 60 pounds, and each carton can carry only one Target stock number, with inner pack and case quantities matching exactly what’s on the purchase order.


#### Slotting Fees & Promotional Funding


Target requires slotting fees, which is a real point of difference from retailers like Costco. Slotting fees depend on type of product, number of SKUs, and number of stores, but they can quickly add up and are something CPG brands don’t always take into consideration.


Target also expects brands to provide promotional funding, which includes contributions toward weekly circulars, Target.com placements, seasonal events, and temporary price reductions. A brand that opts out of funding promotions tends to struggle for the visibility that generates the sell-through Target wants to see.


Brands frequently calculate whether they can afford to produce at the volume Target requires, but don’t run the full math that includes slotting fees, promotional commitments, and the cost of potential chargebacks. A deal that looks profitable on a per-unit basis can look very different once those costs are layered in.

From GFSI requirements to pallet specs, audit documentation, and the production experience to supply the volume needed for mass retail distribution, partnering with The Fresh Factory allows food and beverage brands to hit the ground running.
